title: Generics
subtitle: Write once, use for any type — generic functions, interfaces, and constraints
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Without generics, you'd need to write a separate identity function for string, number, boolean, etc. Or use any — losing type safety. The same logic can't be reused across types without sacrificing checking.
whyItExists.solution: Generics let you write code parameterized by a type variable <T>. The caller provides the type (or TypeScript infers it). The function body is type-checked with T as a placeholder — works for any T.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Any utility function that should work for multiple types (wrap, unwrap, map, filter, find). Any data structure (Stack<T>, Queue<T>, Result<T, E>). Any function that takes a callback and returns the callback's return type.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Don't add a generic type parameter if it only appears in one place — use a specific type instead. If the function only ever works with one type, don't generic-ify it.

explainModes.beginner: Imagine a box that can hold anything. In JavaScript, a box that holds a string and a box that holds a number would both be plain objects. With generics, you can say Box<string> (a box that holds a string) or Box<number> (a box that holds a number). TypeScript then knows exactly what's inside.
explainModes.simple: function identity<T>(arg: T): T — T is a type variable, filled in when called. identity<string>('hello') or identity('hello') (inference). interface Box<T> { value: T }. Constraint: T extends string — T must be a string or subtype. Multiple type params: function pair<A, B>(a: A, b: B): [A, B]. Default type param: interface Container<T = string>.
explainModes.standard: Type inference from arguments: TypeScript infers T from what you pass — identity(42) infers T as number. Constraints with keyof: function getProperty<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K] — K must be a key of T. Generic classes: class Stack<T> { push(item: T): void; pop(): T | undefined }. Conditional generic constraints: T extends Array<infer Item> — extract the element type of an array.
explainModes.technical: Generic type parameter defaults: interface ApiResponse<T = unknown>. Generic type instantiation: type NumberBox = Box<number>. Variance in generics: TypeScript uses structural covariance by default. Explicit variance markers (TS 4.7): interface Reader<out T> (covariant), interface Writer<in T> (contravariant). Bounded polymorphism: function clamp<T extends number>(v: T, min: T, max: T): T — T is constrained but still generic.
explainModes.deepDive: Generic parameter inference vs. instantiation: TypeScript's inference algorithm attempts to unify the types. When it fails, you get 'Could not infer type argument'. Use explicit type argument to fix: fn<MyType>(...). Conditional types over generics: type IsArray<T> = T extends any[] ? true : false. Recursive generics: type DeepPartial<T> = T extends object ? { [K in keyof T]?: DeepPartial<T[K]> } : T. Mapped types with generic constraints: type Pick<T, K extends keyof T> = { [P in K]: T[P] }.

questions.question: What does `function f<T extends { length: number }>(a: T): number` do?
options: f only accepts objects with a length property — strings and arrays qualify
f accepts any type T and returns its length as a number
T extends { length: number } means T must be an array
questions.explanation: The constraint T extends { length: number } means T must have at least a length property that is a number. Strings, arrays, and any object with a length property qualify. This is structural typing — TypeScript doesn't require a specific type, just that the shape matches.

faq.q: When should I add a constraint (T extends Something) vs leave T unconstrained?
faq.a: Add a constraint when you need to use a property or method of T inside the function body. If you just store or return T (identity, wrap, pair), leave it unconstrained. If you call T.length or T.toString(), constrain with T extends { length: number } etc. The constraint expresses what you actually need, and TypeScript enforces it at call sites.
